what_it_does: Serverless computing runs small, short-lived functions in the cloud; each function call often needs data from a slow central database, making response times high. Caching that data locally on each server node is faster, but if multiple nodes cache the same item and one updates it, the others have stale copies — a consistency problem. Concord borrows the same directory-based consistency protocol used inside CPUs to keep their fast on-chip caches synchronized, and adapts it for serverless software caches: a central directory tracks which nodes hold each item, and when one node writes a new value the directory tells the others to discard their copies. Because serverless workloads read far more than they write and function instances start and stop constantly, the protocol is tuned to handle membership changes cheaply. As a bonus, the same infrastructure enables database-style transactions and smart data placement. This is from the abstract only.
